extracted.intended_audience: patent agents and patent agent candidates; inventors with technical backgrounds; IP law students
extracted.subtask_description: Training focused on drafting patent applications (claims, specification, drawings) with attention to enablement, written description, and adapting drafting across multiple jurisdictions including PCT strategy. Includes practical exercises, workshops, mentoring, and a final evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing how claims are to be interpreted in examination and litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers jurisdictional claim construction practices (e.g., USPTO broadest reasonable interpretation, EPO problem-solution approach implications, written description considerations). Emphasis on understanding how different offices construe claim scope to draft appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and dependent claim structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct form and structure for independent and dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamentals of drafting claim sets, how to structure dependencies, appropriate scope allocation between independent and dependent claims, and exercises to practice drafting proper claim chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification writing for enablement and written description
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting the specification to meet enablement and written description requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes providing sufficient disclosure to enable the invention and to support claimed subject-matter; ties to common pitfalls such as insufficient enablement and lack of written description support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and best practices for patent drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers formal drawing requirements and how drawings should support claims and specification; practice exercises to produce drawings complying with various offices' rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting for multiple jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapting drafting style and content to satisfy different national/regional patent office requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative approach: understand USPTO, EPO, JPO, CNIPA and other regional practices (e.g., problem-solution approach, added matter rules, specific support requirements) and draft to avoid office-specific rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international filing strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic considerations for filing under the PCT and managing international prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers timing, claim drafting choices for international protection, and how PCT practice affects later national phase prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoidance of ambiguous or unclear wording in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify examples of ambiguous language, practical exercises to rewrite ambiguous claims into precise language, and explanation of how ambiguity leads to rejections or narrow interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring terms in claims have proper antecedent basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach detection and correction of missing antecedent references to prevent indefiniteness and support issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper transitional phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of correct transitional phrasing (e.g., 'comprising', 'consisting of').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the legal effect of transitional phrases and common mistakes that unintentionally broaden or limit claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding failure to provide enough disclosure to enable the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical exercises demonstrating adequate experimental detail, ranges, and examples to meet enablement across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of written description support
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring claims are supported by the specification's written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training to match claim scope to what is described and to avoid added-matter and written-description rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper means-plus-function language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding or correctly drafting means-plus-function claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain when means-plus-function is interpreted narrowly to the disclosed structure/acts and how to draft alternatives to prevent unintended limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent profanity (limiting language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding inadvertent limiting language that constrains claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify 'patent profanity' examples and demonstrate rewriting to preserve appropriate scope; emphasize common wording that introduces unintended limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to claim multiple invention aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring different inventive aspects are claimed appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach strategies to identify and claim multiple inventive aspects to maximize protection and avoid restriction issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent terminology between specification and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistent terms and definitions across specification and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises to standardize terminology, prevent mismatch that can cause interpretation problems or lack of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to disclose best mode (US only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosing the best mode where required by US law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight jurisdictional specificity: best mode is a US doctrine; discuss when and how to disclose best mode if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology-specific drafting practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailoring drafting practices to specific technology areas (mechanical, electrical, chemical, biotech).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specialized exercises and examples for mechanical, electrical, chemical, and biotech drafting, addressing domain-specific pitfalls and disclosure expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI/software invention drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches to drafting inventions in AI and software domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers particular challenges for software/AI (e.g., technical character, functional claiming, examples, and support) and best practices to improve patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice-oriented outcome: prepare and file successful patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to prepare and file applications that meet formal and substantive requirements for prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program emphasis on practical skills so participants can produce filings likely to proceed through examination with fewer deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice-oriented outcome: draft all-important claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in drafting claims that effectively define and protect inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on drafting claims that balance breadth and support, include dependent claim strategies, and align with prosecution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice-oriented outcome: adapt drafting style across jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in tailoring applications to the expectations of different patent offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training to adapt language, claim formats, and disclosures to anticipate and avoid office-specific objections and rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice-oriented outcome: anticipate common rejection patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to foresee likely examination rejections and draft to reduce them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes learning common rejection patterns per jurisdiction and drafting tactics to mitigate such risks (e.g., claim amendments, support, and argument strategies).
